scope: Production Kotlin encoder, unchanged payload and automatic mask, deterministic no-stress image probes at five save times. These are generated QR images, not app captures or physical phone-camera tests.
decision: Keep the standard size and add a user-controlled larger view. A larger image helped the recorded release payload but did not monotonically improve all cases; it is a fallback, not a claim of universally solved scanning.
findings: The 400px QR recreated from the three RC3 observed payloads exactly matched each actual screenshot QR region pixel-for-pixel.
For the RC3 release payload, OpenCV found no QR candidate at 400px and decoded it at 480px; jsQR matched both.
A combining-mark memo at the standard RC3 timestamp was readable by OpenCV at 400px but not 480px. The prior repeated-Korean case failed OpenCV at both sizes.
All nonempty outputs matched the original payload. Larger-view controls require separate current APK, font-size, lifecycle and state-gate checks.
limitations: No transformations, glare, motion, physical vehicle display or phone-camera scanning were tested in this probe.
No mask overrides or payload changes were selected for production.
512px was probed only at the failing release timestamp and is reported separately rather than pooled with the two display choices.
